blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements per Zscaler cloud for Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA). Zscaler will email a notification to your organization's registered support contacts approximately one week before your cloud is upgraded. To see scheduled maintenance updates for your cloud, visit the Trust Portal.
The following updates were made to the cloud service API:

blocks.item: The following SSL Inspection Settings resources are now available:
The following URL Filtering Policies resources are now available:
The following User Authentication Settings resources are now available:
The GET /urlFilteringRules/lite resource was deprecated and removed.

blocks.text: To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference and API Rate Limit Summary.
The Postman collection was also updated to include new and updated resources. To learn more, see Configuring the Postman REST API Client.

blocks.heading: End of Support for TLS 1.0 & 1.1 for Admin Portal/Cloud Service API

blocks.text: Zscaler no longer supports TLS 1.0 and 1.1 for accessing the ZIA Admin Portal or Cloud Service API. If you are using a browser that does not support TLS 1.2, you must upgrade the browser or use an alternative browser.

The new CIPA Compliance feature helps your organization be in compliance with CIPA requirements. This feature provides a predefined URL filtering rule (CIPA Compliance Rule) and a control (Enable CIPA Compliance) to enable the predefined rule. It also provides a CIPA Compliance Report which gives insights into the traffic and users that are blocked from accessing the prohibited content based on the CIPA Compliance Rule. To learn more, see About CIPA Compliance.

blocks.heading: New File Type Supported for File Type Control

blocks.text: File Type Control now supports Microsoft Visual Studio (.vsix). You can select this file type when adding a File Type Control rule.
To learn more, see Configuring the File Type Control Policy.

ZIA Virtual Service Edge is designed for locations that need the full feature set of a ZIA Public Service Edge (ZEN) in a virtual form factor that is horizontally scalable and requires minimal deployment logistics.
See image.
To learn more, see About Virtual Service Edge and About Virtual Service Edge Clusters.

The OneDrive cloud application is now split into OneDrive and OneDrive (Personal). You can control access to your enterprise and personal OneDrive tenants through the Cloud App Control Policy page, under File Sharing.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding a File Sharing Rule for Cloud App Control and About Microsoft One Click Options.

blocks.heading: Enable IPS Control at a Location or Sub-Location

blocks.text: If Enforce Firewall Control is enabled for a location or sub-location, you can also Enable IPS Control to use signature-based detection to control and protect your traffic inline.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Locations, Configuring Sub-Locations, and About IPS Control.

When configuring admins and admin roles, you can now allow admins access to the Executive Insights App. You can give them access to only the Executive Insights App or both the Admin Portal and the Executive Insights App. The admin's authorized mobile devices also can be viewed in the Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding an Executive Insights App Admin and Editing the Default Executive Insights App Role.
With IPS Control, you can use signature-based detection to control and protect your traffic inline. To learn more, see About IPS Control.

There are multiple ways to visualize and analyze your IPS data. You can use the new IPS Overview dashboard. You can also use the new Threat Category, Threat Name, and IPS Rule Name filters in the Firewall Logs and the IPS Location, IPS Rule, IPS Threat Category, and IPS User data types available with Firewall Insights. To learn more, see About Dashboards, Firewall Insights Logs: Filters, and Firewall Data Types and Filters.
You can also configure your NSS feeds to include data about IPS Rule Names, IPS Actions, Threat Names, and Threat Categories. To learn more, see Adding NSS Feeds for Firewall Logs.

blocks.heading: New Firewall Log Fields for NSS Feed Output

blocks.text: The following Firewall log fields were added to NSS Feeds:
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Firewall Logs.

Zscaler authoritative DNS servers support EDNS0 client subnet options of EDNS0 protocol. To learn more, see RFC 7871: Client Subnet in DNS Queries and RFC 2671: Extension Mechanisms for DNS (EDNS0). These authoritative DNS servers can now accurately identify the origin of the DNS requests by looking into the client subnet options and return more accurate DNS responses based on the user's location.
To learn more, see About Zscaler Authoritative DNS Servers.

The number of allowed tenant domains for Microsoft 365 has increased from 100 to 250, with 64 being the maximum characters per domain. For more information, see Support for Microsoft Tenant Restrictions.

The Sandbox static analysis is now enhanced with machine learning capabilities. Machine learning improves malware detection and increases the accuracy of Sandbox verdicts. You can view the machine learning results in the Sandbox Detail Report.
See image.
You can now use top-level domains (TLD) as criteria in URL filtering policies. Using our new TLD categories, URL filtering policies can match traffic to specific TLDs and act accordingly.
See image.
To learn more, see About TLD Categories and Configuring TLD Categories.

blocks.heading: Enforce Zscaler Client Connector SSL Setting

blocks.text: For Locations, you can now use the Enforce Zscaler Client Connector SSL Setting option to enforce the SSL Inspection setting for Zscaler Client Connector (Z App) and ignore the location's SSL policy for all Zscaler Client Connector traffic.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Locations and Configuring Sub-Locations.
We have added four new predefined DLP dictionaries. These are:

blocks.item: ABA Bank Routing Numbers: This dictionary detects ABA routing transit numbers from the United States.
Individual Taxpayer Registry ID (Brazil): This dictionary detects Individual Taxpayer Registry ID numbers (CPF) from Brazil.
National Health Service Number (UK): This dictionary detects National Health Service (NHS) numbers from the United Kingdom.
Standardized Bank Code (Mexico): This dictionary detects Standardized Bank Code (CLABE) numbers from Mexico.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About DLP Dictionaries and Editing Predefined DLP Dictionaries.

When creating your EDM templates, you can now select ABA Bank Routing Numbers, Individual Taxpayer Registry ID (Brazil), National Health Service Number (UK), and Standardized Bank Code (Mexico) as Data Types. To learn more, see Creating an Exact Data Match Template.

blocks.heading: AES-GCM Support for IPSec VPN Tunnels

blocks.text: Zscaler now supports the following IPSec encryption algorithms for IKE Phase 2:
To learn more, see Supported IPSec VPN Parameters.

The Medical Information DLP dictionary has been enhanced with additional phrases for diseases, treatments, and drugs. In addition, you can now select a Confidence Score Threshold for the National Insurance Numbers (UK) dictionary.
Zscaler now supports ephemeral ECDH with ECDSA signatures for SSL inspection to ensure Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS). To learn more, see Zscaler SSL/TLS Support.

blocks.heading: End User Notification (EUN) for Unauthenticated Traffic

blocks.text: You can now display a caution notification to unauthenticated users sending traffic through a location or sub-location.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Locations, Configuring Sub-Locations, and About Acceptable Use Policy and End User Notifications.
Advanced Threat Protection now supports file format vulnerability protection for PDF documents. To learn more, see Configuring the Advanced Threat Protection Policy.
There is a new Online Gaming category for use in File Type Control. This category is composed of:
You can also select Executable Scripts (py, sh, bat) under the Executable category.

FTP Control is now available to any organization that has the Standard Firewall subscription. This gives you the ability to control FTP over HTTP and native FTP traffic. To learn more, see About FTP Control.

You can now allow or block non-RFC compliant HTTP traffic on HTTP/HTTPS ports. This option is enabled by default for new organizations, but disabled for existing ones. To learn more, see About Advanced Settings.
See image.
You can now allow or block ransomware when configuring the Malware Protection policy. To learn more, see Configuring the Malware Protection Policy.
See image.
Sandbox now supports the following file types when adding a Sandbox Policy rule:
To learn more, see Configuring the Sandbox Policy.
Additional Sandbox enhancements were applied to improve reliability and stability.

blocks.heading: Explicit Proxy Mode Configuration Available for Index Tool VM

blocks.text: You can now choose to configure your Index Tool VM in explicit proxy mode. To learn more, see Configuring the Index Tool.

blocks.heading: Increase to Maximum Number of Dictionaries & Engines

blocks.text: You can now create a maximum of 79 custom DLP dictionaries and 47 custom DLP engines.
The Insights Logs pages have been enhanced to give you a better workflow as you view and define traffic information. These pages contain the following enhancements:

blocks.item: Insights Logs is now its own page, so you can smoothly switch between Insights and Insights Logs.
You can now select the number of records you'd like displayed on the page.
You can now sort through certain columns by ascending or descending order.
You can now search within columns that have the magnifying glass icon next to their name.
At the top of the logs table, you can now see the number of records found between the timeframe you select.

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see About Insights and About Insights Logs.

The new interactive report SSL Traffic Overview allows you view aggregated statistics for metrics logged for SSL transactions. To view the report, go to Analytics > Interactive Reports, and look under Web Activity. To learn more, see About Interactive Reports.
See image.
Items lists now have the following customization options:

blocks.item: Filter the list by searching for a word, phrase, or number contained in an item.
Remove all items from the list or only items from a specific page.
View up to 500 items on a page.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.heading: New Action in Firewall Insights Logs

blocks.text: Zscaler has introduced a new Action in Firewall Insights Logs; Allow due to insufficient app data. This is used when the service's deep packet inspection (DPI) evaluates a Firewall Filtering policy rule containing a Network Application and the session terminates before the DPI can determine the type of traffic or Network Application. To learn more, see Firewall Insights Logs: Filters.
Added four new cloud apps for use in Cloud App Control:

blocks.item: Google Classroom, a Productivity & CRM Tools cloud app
MailBigFile, a File Sharing cloud app
Meetup, a Social Networking cloud app
Zoom, a Collaboration & Online Meetings cloud app

blocks.text: To learn more, see About Cloud App Categories.

blocks.heading: New Controls for RTSP and PPTP Traffic

blocks.text: You can now select RTSP and PPTP as options for Auto Proxy Forwarding for Non-defined Ports. You can use this to send your RTSP and PPTP traffic to the web engine for inspection if it's destined for a non-standard port and doesn't match the predefined network services. To learn more, see About Advanced Settings.
See image.

In addition, if your organization uses a port other than 554 for RTSP traffic or 1723 for PPTP traffic, you can configure the Zscaler service to accept traffic from your custom RTSP and PPTP ports by using the Services Forwarded to RTSP and Services Forwarded to PPTP options. To learn more, see Configuring Custom Ports.
See image.

blocks.heading: New File Types Available for DLP Policies

blocks.text: When creating DLP policy with both Zscaler and external DLP engines you can now select Microsoft Outlook Message (msg) as a File Type. In addition, for policies created with an external DLP engine, you can select Password Protected / Encrypted for use on password protected files. To learn more, see Configuring DLP Policy Rules without Content Inspection.
When creating patterns for your DLP Dictionaries, the \d, \D, \s, \S, \w, and \W character classes are now supported. To learn more, see Defining Patterns for Custom DLP Dictionaries.

blocks.heading: New Ways to Monitor DLP Transactions

blocks.text: We have added two new fields to help you monitor your DLP transactions: DLP MD5 and DLP Identifier. You can find these fields in your DLP Notification Templates, NSS, and Web Insights Logs.
For your DLP Notification Templates, there are two new macros. These are:

blocks.item: ${DLPMD5}: This macro provides the MD5 hash of the file that triggered the DLP rule.
${TRANSACTION_ID}: This macro provides the DLP identifier of the transaction that triggered a DLP rule.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Configuring DLP Notifications.
For your NSS web log feeds, you can add:

blocks.item: %s{dlpmd5}: This field provides the MD5 hash of the file that triggered the DLP rule.
%d{dlpidentifier}: This field provides the DLP identifier of the transaction that triggered the DLP rule.

blocks.text: To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs.
You can use these numbers with the new DLP MD5 and DLP Identifier filters in your Web Insights Logs to help you locate your DLP transactions. To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Filters.
The DLP Dictionaries filter in Web Insights Logs now includes a match count that displays how many times the dictionary was hit.
See image.
For NSS, there is a new %s{dlpdictcount} field which shows the number of times a dictionary was hit. This can be used together with %s{dlpdict} to see how many times a particular dictionary was hit.
There are no changes to the ${DICTIONARIES} macro from DLP Notification Templates as it already displays a match count.

blocks.heading: New Web Log Fields for NSS Feed Output

blocks.text: The following web log fields were added to NSS Feeds:
The existing field %s{ua} will now include the full user agent string. If you'd like the tokenized version, you can add the new field %s{ua_token} to your NSS Feed.
To learn more, see NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs.

The Outlook cloud application is now split into Outlook and Outlook (Personal). You can control access to your enterprise and personal Outlook applications through the Cloud App Control Policy page, under Webmail. To learn how to add a Webmail rule, see Adding a Webmail Rule for Cloud App Control.
See image.

With the Microsoft-Recommended Microsoft 365 One Click Configuration option turned on, Outlook and Outlook (Personal) won’t be SSL bypassed. This allows you to perform SSL inspection to identify phishing attacks and data exfiltration, DLP, Sandbox, and all other security policies Zscaler provides. To learn more, see About Microsoft One Click Options.

blocks.heading: Response Signing SSL Certificate for Identity Proxy

blocks.text: When configuring Identity Proxy settings for cloud apps (Administration > Identity Proxy Settings), You now can choose the signing SSL certificate you want the Identity Proxy to use for signing SAML responses. To learn more, see Configuring the Zscaler Identity Proxy for Cloud Apps.
See image.
We have introduced the ability to schedule regular updates for your Index Template. To learn more, see Creating an Exact Data Match Template.

blocks.heading: SSL Cipher Filters Extended to Encrypted SSL Traffic

blocks.text: The following SSL Cipher Web Insights filters now apply to encrypted SSL traffic (Analytics > Web Insights > Logs):
To learn more, see Web Insights Logs: Filters.

blocks.heading: Terminology Changes on SSL Inspection Page

blocks.text: To enhance clarity, the following field names have changed on the SSL Inspection page (Policy > SSL Inspection):

blocks.item: Do Not Inspect Sessions to these URL Categories is now Exempt These URL Categories from Inspection & Other Policies
Do Not Inspect Sessions to these Hosts is now Exempt These Hosts from Inspection & Other Policies
Do Not Inspect these Applications is now Exempt These Applications from Inspection & Other Policies

blocks.text: On the Advanced Settings page (Administration > Advanced Settings), Enable policies for SSL global exempted domains is now Override Zscaler Global SSL Exemptions List.

With the new Tunnel Insights (Analytics > Tunnel Insights), you can now view IPSec and GRE tunnel data as well as monitor the health and status of your configured tunnels. To learn more, see About Insights and About Insights Logs.
See image.
The following updates were made to the cloud service API:

blocks.item: A /vips endpoint was added that allows you to get a flat list of all virtual IP addresses (VIPs) for your Zscaler cloud. To learn more, see Determining Your Zscaler Data Center VIPs for SD-WAN Integrations and the API Reference.
The rate limit was updated for the following resources:

blocks.text: To learn more, see the API Rate Limit Summary.
The Postman collection was also updated to include new and updated resources. To learn more, see Configuring the Postman REST API Client.
The following ranges and limitations changes were made to the Admin Portal:

blocks.item: Location Groups: You can add a combined total of 256 location groups per organization.
For URL Filtering & Cloud App Control:
Custom URLs: You can add a combined total of 25,000 custom URLs across all policies.
Google App Domains per Request: You can add a combined total of 100 domains, and each domain can have up to 160 characters.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
When adding URLs that count towards the 25,000 custom URL limit, you can now see how many your organization is using and how many are still available to add.
See image.
You can see this information in the following areas within the Admin Portal:

blocks.item: Custom URLs in all URL Categories
Authentication Exempted URLs in Advanced Settings
Optimize the FQDN and Do Not Optimize These FQDN in Advanced Settings
Exempt These Hosts from Inspection & Other Policies in SSL Inspection
Do Not Scan Content from these URLs in Malware Protection and Advanced Threat Protection

blocks.text: The Z-Tunnel is a lightweight, HTTP tunnel that the Zscaler service uses to forward traffic to the ZIA Public Service Edges. Z-Tunnel 2.0 has a tunneling architecture that uses DTLS or TLS to send packets to the Zscaler service. Because of this, Z-Tunnel 2.0 is capable of sending all TCP, UDP and ICMP traffic.
To learn more, see About Z-Tunnel 1.0 & Z-Tunnel 2.0.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Client Connector Portal as IdP

blocks.text: Zscaler Client Connector Portal as IdP (Administration > Authentication Settings) simplifies the configuration process when configuring the Zscaler Client Connector Portal as your IdP. It now automatically performs the necessary configurations with the Zscaler Client Connector IdP URL and certificate. To learn more, see Using the Zscaler Client Connector Portal as an Identity Provider.
See image.

blocks.heading: Perform SSL Inspection for Specific URL Categories

blocks.text: When configuring the SSL Inspection policy, you can now select URL categories you want the service to inspect. To learn more, see Configure the SSL Inspection Policy.
See image.
